To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there exists a prior that induces frequentist coverage in a general class of nonstandard problems.

(a) the prior distribution can be chosen so that the frequentist coverage of the credible set is at least as large as the nominal coverage; and (b) the prior distribution does not need to satisfy the conditions of the asymptotic normality and invariance theorems.

(1) coverage inducing priors (CIPs) exist in general, (2) CIPs can be found by solving a linear system of equations, and (3) CIPs have a natural interpretation in terms of the posterior distribution of the parameter.
